rationale: One major finding: the virtual scroller uses a fixed itemSize of 48px but rows with no email are single-line (~28px) while rows with email are two-line (~44px). Mixed lists will have scroll-height miscalculation causing items to overlap or be unreachable. Fix by making all rows the same height regardless of email presence (e.g. an invisible placeholder on the email line when absent). All 14 acceptance criteria pass; blind lens found no issues; two deferred items (O(n×m) email scan and sticky-cache staleness) are pre-existing patterns with no user-visible bug at current scale.

findings.problem: virtualScrollerOptions.itemSize is set to 48 for all rows, but rows without email are single-line (~28px rendered height) while rows with email are two-line (~44px). With a mixed user list, the virtual scroller's scroll-height calculation will be wrong, causing items to overlap or become unreachable at the bottom of the list.
findings.impact: Users at the bottom of the dropdown list may be visually cut off or inaccessible when the list contains a mix of users with and without email addresses — the common case since the ES path returns no email.
findings.recommendation:
Make all rows the same fixed height regardless of email presence. Simplest fix: always render the email line but hide it when absent using CSS visibility: render `

{option.email || '\u00A0'}

` when email is falsy, so the row height is constant at 48px whether email is present or not.
